name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description: La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The information system manages relationships with suppliers, product proposals, supplier orders, incoming goods, inventory and replenishment, physical and online purchases, deliveries, customer support, and business statistics. Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department. Goods are verified when they arrive at stores. Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured. Customers can purchase products online, pay through multiple methods, and track deliveries. Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms. Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.
rawDescription: La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The information system manages relationships with suppliers, product proposals, supplier orders, incoming goods, inventory and replenishment, physical and online purchases, deliveries, customer support, and business statistics. Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department. Goods are verified when they arrive at stores. Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured. Customers can purchase products online, pay through multiple methods, and track deliveries. Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms. Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.
highLevelGoals: The Supplier aims to easily and effectively submit their product offerings to La Reine Marlene for consideration.
The Supplier seeks assurance that their submitted product proposals are properly evaluated and have a fair chance of being accepted.
The Administrator aims to thoroughly assess and select the most suitable product proposals from suppliers to ensure quality and market relevance.
The Administrator seeks to ensure the information system is correctly configured and operates efficiently to support all business processes.
The Warehouse Staff aims to precisely check and confirm the details of all incoming goods against orders to prevent discrepancies.
The Warehouse Staff seeks to keep precise records of all products in stock to ensure availability and prevent stockouts or overstocking.
The Warehouse Staff aims to automatically or manually trigger and manage the replenishment of products to maintain optimal stock levels.
The Customer aims to easily browse, select, and buy desired products through the online platform.
The Customer seeks to make payments for their online purchases using various secure methods without concerns about data security.
The Customer aims to monitor the real-time status and expected delivery time of their purchased items.
The Customer Support Agent aims to effectively receive, categorize, and process customer inquiries and issues through a ticketing system.
The Customer Support Agent seeks to resolve customer problems within defined deadlines, potentially through automatic assignment and reassignment mechanisms.
The Manager aims to access and analyze detailed data on orders, sales, inventory, and customer support to understand overall business performance.
The Manager seeks to leverage business statistics to identify trends, evaluate performance, and guide strategic planning and operational adjustments.
The Store Clerk aims to quickly and accurately handle customer transactions for products bought directly in the physical store.
The Store Clerk seeks to correctly process various payment methods for immediate sales made by customers in the store.
lowLevelGoals: The Supplier interacts with the system to create and submit a new product proposal, including all necessary details.
The Supplier uploads images associated with a specific product proposal to enhance its presentation.
The Supplier modifies the details of a previously submitted or pending product proposal.
The Supplier checks the current evaluation status of their submitted product proposals.
The Supplier receives automated notifications regarding changes in the evaluation status of their product proposals.
The Supplier views detailed feedback provided by the Administrator on their submitted product proposals.
The Supplier formally accepts the terms and conditions for a product proposal that has been approved by the Administrator.
The Administrator retrieves a comprehensive list of all submitted product proposals, with options to filter by status.
The Administrator accesses the complete details of a specific product proposal for thorough review.
The Administrator changes the status of a product proposal (e.g., 'Approved', 'Rejected') and provides relevant feedback.
The Administrator sends a request to the Supplier for additional information or clarification regarding a specific product proposal.
The Administrator updates specific system-wide parameters, such as tax rates or shipping rules, to maintain optimal operation.
The Administrator assigns or modifies roles and permissions for different users within the system.
The Administrator edits the content and structure of automated system notifications, such as order confirmations.
The Administrator accesses detailed logs of system activities for monitoring, auditing, and troubleshooting purposes.
The Warehouse Staff uses a scanner to record the arrival of a new shipment, initiating the verification process.
The Warehouse Staff fetches the details of a specific purchase order to compare against incoming goods.
The Warehouse Staff logs the exact quantity of a specific item received against a purchase order.
The Warehouse Staff documents any differences between the expected and actual quantities of received items.
The Warehouse Staff marks an entire shipment as fully received and verified after all items have been checked.
The Warehouse Staff adjusts the quantity of a specific product in stock due to receipt, sale, or other inventory changes.
The Warehouse Staff records the physical count of a product in a specific storage location to verify system accuracy.
The Warehouse Staff moves a specified quantity of a product from one storage location to another within the warehouse.
The Warehouse Staff retrieves the real-time quantity of a specific product currently in stock.
The Warehouse Staff flags a quantity of a product as damaged, removing it from available inventory.
The Warehouse Staff accesses a list of products that have fallen below their predefined reorder point.
The Warehouse Staff creates a request to purchase more of a specific product to replenish stock.
The Warehouse Staff approves a generated purchase requisition, allowing it to proceed to the purchasing department.
The Warehouse Staff monitors the current status of an ongoing replenishment order from a supplier.
The Warehouse Staff defines the minimum stock level for a product that triggers a replenishment alert.
The Customer searches and filters products available on the online platform using categories or keywords.
The Customer accesses comprehensive details, specifications, and images for a specific product.
The Customer adds a specified quantity of a product to their online shopping cart.
The Customer modifies the quantity of an item that is already present in their shopping cart.
The Customer deletes a specific item from their online shopping cart.
The Customer initiates the checkout process from their shopping cart to finalize a purchase.
The Customer chooses an existing shipping address or enters a new one for their order.
The Customer chooses their preferred payment method (e.g., credit card, digital wallet) for the online purchase.
The Customer inputs the necessary information for the selected payment method to complete the transaction.
The Customer enters and applies a promotional or discount code to their order during checkout.
The Customer authorizes and finalizes the payment for their online order.
The Customer receives a notification confirming the successful processing of their payment.
The Customer accesses a list of all their past and current online orders.
The Customer retrieves the current processing and shipping status of a particular order.
The Customer sees estimated delivery dates and tracking numbers for their purchased items.
The Customer gets alerts when the status of their order delivery changes (e.g., 'Shipped', 'Out for Delivery').
The Customer Support Agent accesses a list of newly submitted customer support tickets, with filtering options.
The Customer Support Agent takes ownership of an unassigned support ticket to begin processing it.
The Customer Support Agent changes the status of a support ticket (e.g., 'Open', 'In Progress', 'Resolved').
The Customer Support Agent adds internal notes or comments to a support ticket for documentation or collaboration.
The Customer Support Agent assigns a category or tag to a support ticket for better organization and routing.
The Customer Support Agent filters and views support tickets based on their assigned priority level.
The Customer Support Agent marks a ticket for escalation to a higher-level support agent or manager due to complexity or urgency.
The Customer Support Agent sends a direct message or update to the customer regarding their support ticket.
The Customer Support Agent marks a support ticket as resolved and provides details of the resolution.
The Customer Support Agent transfers a support ticket to another customer support agent for handling.
The Manager creates a report detailing sales performance over a specified date range and product category.
The Manager accesses a report showing current inventory levels, including items with low stock.
The Manager obtains statistics on customer support performance, such as average resolution time and ticket volume.
The Manager exports specific business data (e.g., sales, inventory) into a CSV format for external analysis.
The Manager accesses a high-level summary dashboard displaying key business metrics and performance indicators.
The Manager compares sales data between two different time periods to identify trends and changes.
The Manager generates a list of the best-selling products within a specified timeframe to inform purchasing and marketing strategies.
The Manager reviews aggregated customer feedback to identify common issues, sentiments, and areas for improvement.
The Manager uses historical data to predict future inventory requirements for specific product categories.
The Manager assesses the effectiveness of a specific marketing campaign based on sales data and other relevant metrics.
The Store Clerk adds a product to the current in-store transaction by scanning its barcode.
The Store Clerk finds and adds a product to the current transaction by searching its name in the system.
The Store Clerk modifies the quantity of an item already added to the current in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk removes a specific item from the current in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk applies a discount to a specific item within the current in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk computes the final total amount due for the current in-store transaction, including taxes and discounts.
The Store Clerk records a cash payment received for an in-store transaction and calculates change.
The Store Clerk initiates and processes a credit or debit card payment for an in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk applies a gift card as a payment method for an in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk prints or emails a receipt for a completed in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk processes a product return, initiating a refund or store credit based on the original transaction.

The goals are functional in nature, focusing on the 'what' and 'why' of the system's capabilities without delving into technical implementation details. There are no contradictions with the description, and no significant functional areas appear to be omitted.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for REWRITE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original goal 'Efficiently submit product proposals' is a workflow fragment (submission phase) of the broader supplier intention to manage their product offerings. The sibling goal 'Ensure proposal evaluation and acceptance' covers the post-submission phase (evaluation/acceptance). Together, these two goals fragment the single end-to-end stakeholder outcome of 'Managing Product Proposals' (creating, submitting, and tracking status). According to the consolidation audit, if the hierarchy is fragmented and no single sibling acts as a valid umbrella, the broadest suitable goal should be rewritten to encompass the full lifecycle. 'Efficiently submit product proposals' is the primary action initiated by the supplier and is the most suitable candidate to be expanded into an umbrella goal covering creation, submission, and status tracking, thereby subsuming the narrower 'Ensure proposal evaluation and acceptance' goal (which would then be removed or merged). Keeping it as is leaves the hierarchy fragmented.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The information system manages relationships with suppliers, product proposals, supplier orders, incoming goods, inventory and replenishment, physical and online purchases, deliveries, customer support, and business statistics. Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department. Goods are verified when they arrive at stores. Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured. Customers can purchase products online, pay through multiple methods, and track deliveries. Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms. Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.

Rewrite the functional intention for actor 'Supplier' using this focus: Express one end-to-end goal covering the creation, submission, and status tracking of product proposals.

branch_004.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Accurately verify incoming goods' is supported by the project description ('Goods are verified when they arrive at stores') and the actor description ('Verifies incoming goods'). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Process Goods Receipt' suggests a broader scope that might include logging and finalizing, but the specific intent of 'verification' is a distinct, critical quality control step documented in the system. It is not redundant with 'Maintain accurate inventory levels' (which focuses on stock records) or 'Ensure timely stock replenishment' (which focuses on ordering). Verification is a prerequisite for accurate inventory updates but represents a specific operational outcome (confirming goods match orders) that is independently valuable and documented. It does not document specific mechanisms such as 'scanning', 'retrieving purchase order details' as a distinct user action, 'recording item quantity' as a separate step from verification, or 'confirming full shipment receipt'. While these are conventional steps in a warehouse management system, the instructions strictly prohibit inferring operations (like scanning, specific CRUD variants, or status transitions) unless explicitly entailed by the documentation. The documentation supports the general capability of 'verifying incoming goods' but does not support the specific granular operations listed in the LLGs. branch_005.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for REWRITE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Maintain accurate inventory levels' is supported by the documentation, which states that 'Inventory is monitored'. However, the actor description for Warehouse Staff explicitly lists three distinct responsibilities: 'Verifies incoming goods, monitors inventory, and manages replenishment.' The current hierarchy fragments these into three separate HLGs: 'Accurately verify incoming goods', 'Maintain accurate inventory levels', and 'Ensure timely stock replenishment'. These three goals operate on the same artifact (inventory/stock) and jointly realize the single end-to-end stakeholder outcome of managing warehouse inventory. 'Maintaining accurate inventory levels' is not an independently satisfiable outcome separate from verification and replenishment; rather, it is the continuous state resulting from the combination of verifying incoming goods and managing replenishment. Therefore, the hierarchy is fragmented. The broadest suitable goal to serve as an umbrella for these related capabilities is 'Manage Warehouse Inventory' (or similar), which encompasses monitoring, verification, and replenishment. The original goal is too narrow and represents a fragment of the broader inventory management intention.

branch_007.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The Customer actor has three distinct, independently satisfiable stakeholder outcomes documented in the description: purchasing products online, making payments, and tracking deliveries. The original HLG 'Conveniently purchase products online' covers the browsing and selection phase. The sibling HLG 'Securely complete payments' covers the transactional phase. The sibling HLG 'Accurately track order deliveries' covers the post-purchase phase. These are not fragments of a single monolithic workflow that must be merged; rather, they represent distinct value propositions (acquisition, financial settlement, logistics visibility) that can be satisfied independently (e.g., a customer might track a delivery without re-purchasing, or pay for an item without browsing new ones). The original goal is supported by the description ('Customers can purchase products online') and is appropriately scoped to the browsing/selection intent, distinct from the payment and tracking intents. Therefore, it should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs accurately decompose the parent HLG 'Conveniently purchase products online' into essential, documented capabilities. The project description explicitly states that 'Customers can purchase products online'. The LLGs cover the standard and necessary steps for this process: browsing (llg_001), viewing details (llg_002), managing the cart (llg_003, llg_004, llg_005), and initiating the purchase by proceeding to checkout and selecting a shipping address (llg_006, llg_007). These steps are necessarily entailed by the goal of purchasing products online. The sibling HLG 'Securely complete payments' correctly handles the payment execution, so the current LLGs appropriately stop at the initiation of checkout/shipping selection without duplicating payment processing. No unsupported or misleading LLGs are present, and no essential capabilities for the online purchase workflow are missing.

branch_006.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Conveniently purchase products online' is supported by the project description and the actor's role. It represents a distinct stakeholder outcome (acquiring goods via the web channel) that is separate from 'Securely complete payments' (financial transaction security) and 'Accurately track order deliveries' (post-purchase logistics). While 'purchase' can semantically encompass payment, in requirements engineering, the convenience of the browsing/selection process and the security of the payment process are often treated as distinct quality attributes or functional areas. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Customers to Purchase Products Online' is semantically equivalent to the original. There is no broader sibling goal for the Customer that encompasses the entire online shopping experience (browsing + payment + tracking) as a single umbrella, so this goal is not redundant. It is appropriately scoped as a primary functional goal for the Customer actor. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs accurately decompose the parent goal 'Conveniently purchase products online' into essential steps: browsing (llg_001), viewing details (llg_002), cart management (llg_003, llg_004, llg_005), initiating checkout (llg_006), and selecting shipping address (llg_007). All these capabilities are explicitly supported by the project description ('Customers can purchase products online') and the parent HLG description ('easily browse, select, and buy'). The sibling HLG 'Securely complete payments' covers the payment transaction itself, so excluding specific payment method selection from this HLG is correct to avoid duplication. The sibling 'Accurately track order deliveries' covers post-purchase tracking, so excluding that is also correct. No essential capabilities are missing, and no LLGs are unsupported.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale:
Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The project description outlines the following functional areas: supplier proposals, incoming goods verification, inventory monitoring, replenishment, online purchases, payments, delivery tracking, customer support, and business statistics. 

1. **Supplier**: Covered by 'Manage Product Proposals' and 'Ensure proposal evaluation and acceptance'.
2. **Administrator**: Covered by 'Effectively evaluate supplier proposals' and 'Maintain optimal system configuration'.
3. **Warehouse Staff**: The description states 'Goods are verified when they arrive at stores. Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured.' The current HLGs are 'Accurately verify incoming goods', 'Manage Warehouse Inventory', and 'Ensure timely stock replenishment'. Although 'Manage Warehouse Inventory' was previously flagged for redundancy in the previous turn's context, in the context of this specific audit for *missing* goals, the core responsibilities (verification, monitoring/inventory management, replenishment) are explicitly covered by the existing HLGs. The retired goal 'Maintain accurate inventory levels' is semantically entailed by 'Manage Warehouse Inventory' (which includes monitoring) and 'Ensure timely stock replenishment'. There is no uncovered functional requirement for Warehouse Staff.
4. **Customer**: Covered by 'Conveniently purchase products online', 'Securely complete payments', and 'Accurately track order deliveries'.
5. **Customer Support Agent**: Covered by 'Efficiently manage customer support requests' and 'Ensure timely resolution of customer issues'.
6. **Manager**: Covered by 'Gain comprehensive business insights' and 'Make informed strategic decisions'.
7. **Store Clerk**: Covered by 'Efficiently process in-store purchases' and 'Accurately handle in-store payments'.

All explicit actor-level functional requirements from the description are mapped to existing High-Level Goals. No new gaps are identified.

If 'Purchase' implies the entire flow up to payment, then 'Payment' is a sub-goal. If 'Purchase' is just adding to cart, it's narrow. The description says 'browse, select, and buy'. missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale:
Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The current HLG list comprehensively covers all explicit functional requirements and actor-level responsibilities documented in the project description. 

1. **Supplier**: 'Manage Product Proposals' and 'Ensure proposal evaluation and acceptance' cover the submission and monitoring of proposals.
2. **Administrator**: 'Effectively evaluate supplier proposals' and 'Maintain optimal system configuration' cover the evaluation and configuration management.
3. **Warehouse Staff**: 'Accurately verify incoming goods', 'Manage Warehouse Inventory', and 'Ensure timely stock replenishment' cover the verification, monitoring, and replenishment processes.
4. **Customer**: 'Conveniently purchase products online', 'Securely complete payments', and 'Accurately track order deliveries' cover the online purchase, payment, and tracking workflows.
5. **Customer Support Agent**: 'Efficiently manage customer support requests' and 'Ensure timely resolution of customer issues' cover the ticketing, assignment, and resolution processes.
6. **Manager**: 'Gain comprehensive business insights' and 'Make informed strategic decisions' cover the analysis of business data.
7. **Store Clerk**: 'Efficiently manage complete in-store sales transactions' and 'Accurately handle in-store payments' cover the in-store purchase assistance and payment processing. The retired HLG 'Efficiently process in-store purchases' is fully entailed by the current 'Efficiently manage complete in-store sales transactions', which explicitly includes handling all aspects of an in-store purchase.

No explicit functional requirements are left uncovered. All documented actor capabilities are mapped to existing HLGs.

The description states that 'Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department' but does not mention a mechanism for the Administrator to request additional information or clarification from the Supplier. While this is a plausible workflow step, it is not entailed by the provided documentation. According to the strict evaluation criteria, conventional or useful operations that are not explicitly documented or necessarily entailed must be removed. The current LLGs stop at 'Proceed to checkout' and 'Select shipping address', omitting the essential capability of selecting a payment method and completing the payment transaction. branch_010.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Warehouse Inventory' is supported by the project description, which states that 'Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured' and 'Goods are verified when they arrive at stores'. The actor description explicitly lists 'Verifies incoming goods, monitors inventory, and manages replenishment' as the responsibilities of Warehouse Staff. The goal correctly aggregates these related capabilities (verification, monitoring, replenishment) into a single coherent stakeholder outcome for maintaining stock levels. It is not fragmented into separate HLGs for each step, nor is it redundant with other goals for this actor (as no other Warehouse Staff HLGs exist in the current list). The granularity is appropriate for a high-level goal representing the end-to-end inventory management process for this actor. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) contain several capabilities that are not explicitly supported by the project description or the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) description. Specifically: 1) 'RecordIncomingShipmentDetails' (llg_001) implies recording supplier/manifest details, but the documentation only states 'Goods are verified when they arrive at stores' and 'Inventory is monitored', without specifying shipment detail recording. 2) 'ScanReceivedItemBarcode' (llg_002) specifies a barcode scanning mechanism, which is a specific implementation detail not mentioned in the documentation. 3) 'MarkPurchaseOrderAsReceived' (llg_004) references 'Purchase Orders', but the documentation mentions 'supplier orders' in the context of supplier relationships and 'replenishment' for inventory, not explicitly linking warehouse verification to 'Purchase Orders' as a distinct entity to be marked. 4) 'GenerateInventoryStatusReport' (llg_006) and 'InitiateInventoryCycleCount' (llg_007) are specific operational features (reporting and cycle counting) not explicitly entailed by 'monitors inventory'. While monitoring implies checking levels, generating detailed reports and initiating formal cycle counts are distinct functionalities not documented. 5) 'GenerateReplenishmentOrderProposal' (llg_010) and 'SubmitApprovedReplenishmentOrder' (llg_011) imply a complex proposal/approval workflow for replenishment. The documentation states 'automatic replenishment can be configured', which suggests a system-driven process rather than a manual proposal generation and submission workflow by warehouse staff. The core documented capabilities are verifying incoming goods, monitoring inventory, and managing (configuring/triggering) replenishment. The current LLGs over-specify the mechanisms (barcodes, reports, cycle counts, manual proposals) beyond the documented scope.

branch_011.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently manage complete in-store sales transactions' is supported by the project description, which mentions 'physical and online purchases' and the actor description, which states the Store Clerk 'Assists customers with in-store purchases, processes payments, and handles immediate sales.' However, the hierarchy is fragmented. There is a sibling HLG 'Accurately handle in-store payments' for the same actor. 'Handling payments' is a specific phase of the broader 'sales transaction' workflow. The original HLG explicitly claims to cover 'all aspects... from assisting with product selection to accurately processing various payment methods,' which entails the sibling goal. According to the consolidation audit, if a broader sibling already entails the original goal (or if the original is the broader umbrella but the hierarchy is fragmented such that the original is the most comprehensive expression of the end-to-end outcome), we must ensure the hierarchy is not redundant. Here, the original HLG is the broader, end-to-end goal that encompasses the payment processing. The sibling 'Accurately handle in-store payments' is a workflow fragment of the 'complete in-store sales transaction'. Therefore, the original HLG is the correct umbrella goal. The sibling should ideally be removed or merged, but for the evaluation of *this* specific HLG, it is the valid, supported, and appropriately scoped end-to-end intention. It is not redundant because it is the broader goal, not the fragment. It is not fragmented because it covers the whole process. Thus, it should be kept as the primary goal for this actor's sales activity. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the workflow for managing in-store sales transactions, including product search, retrieval, adding/removing items, adjusting quantities, applying discounts, processing various payment methods (cash, card, gift card), finalizing the transaction, generating receipts, and voiding transactions. All these capabilities are explicitly supported by the parent HLG description ('assisting with product selection', 'accurately processing various payment methods', 'complete sales experience') and the actor description ('Assists customers with in-store purchases, processes payments, and handles immediate sales'). The project description confirms that the system manages 'physical and online purchases' and that customers can 'pay through multiple methods'. The specific payment methods (cash, card, gift card) are standard interpretations of 'various payment methods' in a retail context and are not contradicted by the documentation. The sibling HLG 'Accurately handle in-store payments' overlaps with the payment processing LLGs, but since the parent HLG explicitly includes 'processing various payment methods' as part of the 'complete in-store sales transaction', these LLGs are correctly placed under the broader transaction management goal. There are no unsupported or misleading LLGs, and no essential capabilities are missing.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale:
Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. A requirement-by-requirement audit confirms that all explicit functional responsibilities in the project description are covered by the current High-Level Goals. 

1. **Supplier**: 'Submits product proposals' is covered by 'Manage Product Proposals'. The retired goal 'Ensure proposal evaluation and acceptance' is redundant as the outcome (evaluation) is handled by the Administrator's HLG, and the Supplier's primary action is submission.
2. **Administrator**: 'Evaluates supplier proposals' is covered by 'Effectively evaluate supplier proposals'. 'Manages system configurations' is covered by 'Maintain optimal system configuration'.
3. **Warehouse Staff**: 'Verifies incoming goods', 'monitors inventory', and 'manages replenishment' are all entailed by the comprehensive HLG 'Manage Warehouse Inventory', which explicitly mentions verifying incoming goods, monitoring inventory, and managing replenishment. The retired specific goals ('Accurately verify incoming goods', 'Ensure timely stock replenishment', 'Maintain accurate inventory levels') are sub-components of this broader goal and do not represent independent stakeholder outcomes requiring separate HLGs.
4. **Customer**: 'Purchases products online' is covered by 'Conveniently purchase products online'. 'Tracks deliveries' is covered by 'Accurately track order deliveries'. 'Makes payments' is part of the purchase transaction; while 'Securely complete payments' was retired, the payment process is inherently part of the 'Conveniently purchase products online' workflow for online customers, and no separate explicit requirement for a distinct payment management goal for online customers (distinct from in-store) is evidenced as a separate stakeholder outcome beyond the purchase itself.
5. **Customer Support Agent**: 'Manages customer support requests and tickets' is covered by 'Efficiently manage customer support requests'. The retired 'Ensure timely resolution' is a quality attribute of the management process, not a separate functional goal.
6. **Manager**: 'Analyzes business data' is covered by 'Gain comprehensive business insights' and 'Make informed strategic decisions'.
7. **Store Clerk**: 'Assists customers with in-store purchases' and 'handles immediate sales' are covered by 'Efficiently manage complete in-store sales transactions'. 'Processes payments' is covered by 'Accurately handle in-store payments'.

No explicit functional requirements are left uncovered. The current HLGs provide complete coverage of the documented actor responsibilities.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Effectively evaluate supplier proposals' is supported by the project description ('Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department') and the actor description ('Evaluates supplier proposals'). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Product Proposals' is too generic for the Administrator, as it conflates the evaluation process with the broader lifecycle management which is primarily the Supplier's concern (submitting/monitoring) or a system-wide state. The Administrator's specific stakeholder outcome is the assessment and selection of proposals. This goal is distinct from 'Maintain optimal system configuration' (the other Administrator HLG). It is not a mere workflow fragment of a sibling HLG because the Supplier's HLG focuses on submission and monitoring, while the Administrator's HLG focuses on the internal decision-making process (evaluation/selection). Therefore, the original goal is correctly scoped and supported. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs cover the core aspects of evaluating proposals: listing (llg_001), viewing details (llg_002), and updating status/feedback (llg_003). However, llg_004 ('Request clarification on proposal') is not explicitly supported by the project description or the actor description. The documentation states that suppliers submit proposals and the administration evaluates them, but it does not mention a mechanism for the administrator to request additional information or clarification from the supplier. While this is a common workflow step, it is an inferred capability not entailed by the provided text. According to the strict evaluation criteria, unsupported additions must be flagged. Therefore, the decomposition requires regeneration to remove the unsupported LLG.

The bottom-up reconstruction 'Oversee and Configure System Operations' aligns well with the documented capabilities (configuring parameters, managing access, notifications, monitoring). It is not a fragment of another goal but a core administrative function. While 'Modify system configuration parameters' (llg_001) is a reasonable interpretation of 'manages system configurations', the other LLGs (llg_002, llg_003, llg_004) infer standard administrative functions (access control, notification customization, auditing) that are not documented. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Product Proposals' accurately captures the end-to-end intention of the Supplier actor as described in the project documentation. The documentation states that 'Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department.' The goal encompasses the creation, submission, and monitoring of these proposals, which constitutes the complete lifecycle of the Supplier's interaction with the system regarding this artifact. The documentation states suppliers 'submit proposals,' which entails the creation and submission of the proposal content, but does not explicitly document a distinct 'draft' state or a separate step for adding details versus creating the proposal. While plausible, the specific workflow of 'drafting' is an inferred implementation detail rather than a documented capability. 2) 'Attach supporting documents to a proposal draft' (llg_003) is entirely unsupported. The documentation says proposals are 'evaluated', which implies a result, but does not explicitly state that feedback is provided or that it is viewable specifically for rejections. More critically, the combination of unsupported drafting steps and unsupported attachments constitutes a material defect. The core documented capabilities are submitting a proposal and monitoring its status. The LLGs introduce an unsupported complexity (drafting/attachments) that is not in the source text. Therefore, regeneration is required to remove unsupported operations and align strictly with the documented 'submit' and 'monitor' actions.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale:
Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. A requirement-by-requirement audit confirms that all explicit functional responsibilities in the project description are covered by the current High-Level Goals. 

1. **Supplier**: 'Submits product proposals' is covered by 'Manage Product Proposals'. The retired goal 'Ensure proposal evaluation and acceptance' is not a distinct functional requirement for the supplier (who only submits); the evaluation is the Administrator's responsibility, covered by 'Effectively evaluate supplier proposals'.
2. **Administrator**: 'Evaluates supplier proposals' is covered by 'Effectively evaluate supplier proposals'. 'Manages system configurations' is covered by 'Maintain optimal system configuration'.
3. **Warehouse Staff**: 'Verifies incoming goods', 'monitors inventory', and 'manages replenishment' are all covered by the comprehensive HLG 'Manage Warehouse Inventory'. The retired goals ('Accurately verify incoming goods', 'Maintain accurate inventory levels', 'Ensure timely stock replenishment') are sub-tasks or aspects of this single coherent workflow and do not represent independent stakeholder outcomes requiring separate HLGs.
4. **Customer**: 'Purchases products online' is covered by 'Conveniently purchase products online'. 'Tracks deliveries' is covered by 'Accurately track order deliveries'. The retired goal 'Securely complete payments' is a technical/non-functional aspect of the purchase process or part of the payment processing handled by the system/clerk, not a distinct customer-facing functional goal separate from the purchase itself in this context (online payment is part of the online purchase flow).

high_level_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Effectively evaluate supplier proposals' is fully supported by the project description, which states that 'Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department.' The Administrator's role explicitly includes evaluating these proposals. The goal represents a distinct, independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome (the evaluation and selection of proposals) that is separate from the Supplier's goal of managing/submitting them or the Administrator's other goal of maintaining system configuration. It is not a mere workflow fragment of a broader goal, as the evaluation process is a core business function with its own lifecycle (review, assessment, decision). The reconstruction 'Evaluate Product Proposals' is semantically equivalent but less descriptive of the intent ('effectively' and 'thoroughly assess' capture the quality aspect better). Therefore, the original goal is appropriate and should be kept.

low_level_evaluation.rationale:
Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) provide a complete and supported decomposition of the High-Level Goal 'Effectively evaluate supplier proposals'. 

1. **llg_001 (List all product proposals)**: Supported by the need to 'retrieve a comprehensive list' to begin evaluation. This is a necessary precondition for assessing available options.
2. **llg_002 (View detailed product proposal)**: Supported by the HLG description 'thoroughly assess' and the project context where proposals contain specifications and pricing. Reviewing details is essential for evaluation.
3. **llg_003 (Update product proposal status)**: Supported by the HLG description 'select the most suitable product proposals'. Selection implies a decision (approve/reject) which must be recorded in the system. The sibling HLG for Suppliers mentions 'monitor the status', implying that the status is a tracked attribute that changes based on the Administrator's evaluation. Updating the status is the concrete action that realizes the 'selection' part of the HLG.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale:
Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. A requirement-by-requirement audit confirms that all explicit functional responsibilities in the project description are covered by the current High-Level Goals (HLGs). 

1. **Supplier**: 'Submits product proposals' is covered by 'Manage Product Proposals'. The retired goal 'Efficiently submit product proposals' is subsumed by this current HLG, which encompasses the creation and submission workflow.
2. **Administrator**: 'Evaluates supplier proposals' is covered by 'Effectively evaluate supplier proposals'. 'Manages system configurations' is covered by 'Maintain optimal system configuration'.
3. **Warehouse Staff**: 'Verifies incoming goods', 'monitors inventory', and 'manages replenishment' are all explicitly included in the description of 'Manage Warehouse Inventory'. The retired goals regarding verification and replenishment are fully entailed by this comprehensive HLG.
4. **Customer**: 'Purchases products online' is covered by 'Conveniently purchase products online'. 'Tracks deliveries' is covered by 'Accurately track order deliveries'. The retired goal 'Securely complete payments' is a step within the online purchase workflow and does not constitute a separate high-level outcome distinct from the purchase itself in this context, as payment is integral to completing the online purchase.
5. **Customer Support Agent**: 'Manages customer support requests and tickets' is covered by 'Efficiently manage customer support requests'. The retired goal regarding timely resolution is an aspect of efficient management and is not a distinct functional capability requiring its own HLG.
6. **Manager**: 'Analyzes business data' is covered by 'Gain comprehensive business insights'. The retired goal 'Make informed strategic decisions' is the outcome of the analysis, not a separate system function.
7. **Store Clerk**: 'Assists customers with in-store purchases, processes payments, and handles immediate sales' is covered by 'Efficiently manage complete in-store sales transactions'. The retired goals regarding specific payment handling are subsumed by the complete transaction management.

No explicit functional requirements are left uncovered. The current HLGs provide complete coverage of the documented actor-level responsibilities.

The original High-Level Goal 'Conveniently purchase products online' is supported by the project description, which states that 'Customers can purchase products online'. The goal captures the core stakeholder intention of the Customer actor regarding the online shopping process (browsing, selecting, buying). It is distinct from the sibling goal 'Accurately track order deliveries', which focuses on the post-purchase logistics phase. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Customers to Shop for Products Online' is semantically equivalent to the original goal. The original goal is appropriately scoped as an independent end-to-end functional outcome for the Customer actor, covering the transactional aspect of the system. It is not a fragment of a broader goal, nor is it redundant with other goals. Therefore, it should be kept. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) cover the browsing, selection, and cart management aspects of the parent goal 'Conveniently purchase products online'. However, the project description explicitly states that 'Customers can purchase products online, pay through multiple methods'. The current LLGs end at 'Proceed to checkout' and 'Select shipping address', but they do not include the essential capability of selecting a payment method or completing the payment. Without a goal for payment selection/processing, the decomposition is incomplete regarding the 'buy' aspect of the parent goal, as the transaction is not finalized without payment. Therefore, an essential capability is missing.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The information system manages relationships with suppliers, product proposals, supplier orders, incoming goods, inventory and replenishment, physical and online purchases, deliveries, customer support, and business statistics. Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department. Goods are verified when they arrive at stores. Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured. Customers can purchase products online, pay through multiple methods, and track deliveries. Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms. Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Conveniently purchase products online' is fully supported by the project description, which states that customers can purchase products online and pay through multiple methods. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Customers to Purchase Products Online' aligns with this intention. The goal is appropriately scoped as an independent stakeholder outcome, distinct from 'Accurately track order deliveries' (which covers the post-purchase phase) and 'Efficiently manage complete in-store sales transactions' (which covers the physical store context). It is not a redundant fragment of a broader sibling goal, as no other Customer HLG covers the online purchasing process itself. The granularity is correct for a High-Level Goal, representing the complete end-to-end online purchase intention. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) cover the browsing, selection, and cart management phases of the online purchase process. However, the project description explicitly states that customers can 'pay through multiple methods'. The parent HLG 'Conveniently purchase products online' encompasses the entire purchase transaction, which is incomplete without the payment step. The current LLGs end at 'Proceed to checkout' and 'Select shipping address', omitting the essential capability of selecting a payment method and completing the payment. This is a material omission of an explicitly documented capability required to fulfill the parent goal. Therefore, the LLGs must be regenerated to include payment processing.

branch_003.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently manage customer support requests' is fully supported by the project description, which states that 'Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms.' The actor 'Customer Support Agent' is explicitly described as managing these requests. The goal represents a complete, end-to-end functional outcome for this actor (managing the ticket lifecycle from receipt to resolution). There are no other High-Level Goals for the Customer Support Actor that would make this redundant or fragmented. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Process Customer Support Tickets' is semantically equivalent but slightly less descriptive of the management aspect (assignment, deadlines) implied by the original. Therefore, the original goal is accurate, well-scoped, and should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain several capabilities that are not explicitly supported by the project description. Specifically, 'Add note to ticket' (llg_004) is not mentioned in the documentation, which only lists automatic assignment, response deadlines, and reassignment mechanisms. 'Categorize support ticket' (llg_005) is also not explicitly documented; while 'categorize' appears in the HLG description, the project description does not mention categorization as a feature of the ticketing system. 'Assign ticket to self' (llg_002) is partially supported by 'automatic assignment' and 'reassignment', but the specific action of an agent manually taking ownership of an unassigned ticket is not explicitly detailed, though it is a reasonable interpretation of managing tickets. However, the most significant issue is the absence of a capability to 'Respond to customer support requests' or 'Resolve customer support requests', which is the core purpose of managing support tickets. The description mentions 'response deadlines', implying that responses are a key part of the workflow, but no LLG explicitly covers the act of responding to or resolving the customer's issue. Therefore, the LLGs need to be regenerated to remove unsupported features (notes, categorization) and include the essential capability of responding/resolving tickets.

branch_005.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Product Proposals' is well-supported by the project description, which states that 'Suppliers submit proposals'. The goal correctly captures the end-to-end intention of the Supplier actor: creating, submitting, and monitoring the status of these proposals. It is not a fragmented workflow step but rather the complete lifecycle management of the supplier's primary artifact (the product proposal). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Supplier Product Proposals' is semantically equivalent to the original, just slightly more specific. There are no other HLGs for the Supplier actor that would make this redundant. The granularity is appropriate for a stakeholder outcome. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) contain several capabilities that are not explicitly supported by the project description or necessarily entailed by the parent HLG 'Manage Product Proposals'. Specifically: 1) 'Create a new product proposal draft' (llg_001) and 'Add product details to a proposal draft' (llg_002) imply a multi-step drafting and editing workflow. The description only states 'Suppliers submit proposals', which entails the creation and submission of the proposal content, but does not explicitly document a distinct 'draft' state or iterative editing capability separate from the submission act. 2) 'Attach supporting documents to a proposal draft' (llg_003) is entirely unsupported; the description makes no mention of file uploads, images, or attachments. 3) 'View evaluation feedback for a rejected proposal' (llg_007) is partially redundant with llg_006 but specifically highlights 'rejected' status. While the description mentions proposals are 'evaluated', it does not explicitly state that feedback/reasons are provided to the supplier upon rejection, nor does it distinguish a specific 'rejected' view from general status monitoring. More critically, the core capability of 'submitting' the proposal is present (llg_004), and 'monitoring status' is present (llg_005, llg_006). However, the inclusion of unsupported features like document attachment and explicit draft management constitutes a material defect. The essential capabilities are: Submitting a product proposal and Monitoring the status of submitted proposals. The current LLGs include unsupported additions (llg_003) and potentially over-specified workflow steps (llg_001, llg_002) that go beyond the simple 'submit' action described. Therefore, regeneration is required to remove unsupported capabilities and align strictly with the documented scope.

branch_006.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Warehouse Inventory' is fully supported by the project description, which states that 'Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured' and that 'Goods are verified when they arrive at stores.' The actor description for Warehouse Staff explicitly lists 'Verifies incoming goods, monitors inventory, and manages replenishment.' The goal correctly encapsulates the end-to-end responsibility of the Warehouse Staff actor regarding stock levels. It is not fragmented; rather, it serves as the umbrella for the related activities of receiving, monitoring, and replenishing. There are no other HLGs for the Warehouse Staff actor that would make this redundant. The bottom-up reconstruction is semantically identical. The granularity is appropriate for a stakeholder outcome. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain several unsupported capabilities that go beyond the explicit documentation. Specifically, 'RecordIncomingShipmentDetails' (llg_001) and 'ScanReceivedItemBarcode' (llg_002) introduce specific data fields and hardware interactions (barcodes, manifests) not mentioned in the description, which only states that 'Goods are verified'. 'MarkPurchaseOrderAsReceived' (llg_004) implies a specific status transition for purchase orders that is not documented. 'InitiateInventoryCycleCount' (llg_007) and 'RecordInventoryCountDiscrepancy' (llg_008) introduce cycle counting and discrepancy resolution workflows that are not entailed by 'monitors inventory'. 'GenerateReplenishmentOrderProposal' (llg_010) and 'SubmitApprovedReplenishmentOrder' (llg_011) imply a complex approval and proposal workflow for replenishment that is not supported; the description only states that 'automatic replenishment can be configured'. 'TrackReplenishmentOrderStatus' (llg_012) is also unsupported as tracking is explicitly assigned to customers for deliveries, not warehouse staff for replenishment orders. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Warehouse Inventory' is fully supported by the project description, which states that 'Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured' and that 'Goods are verified when they arrive at stores.' The actor description for Warehouse Staff explicitly lists 'Verifies incoming goods, monitors inventory, and manages replenishment.' The goal correctly encapsulates the end-to-end responsibility of the Warehouse Staff actor regarding stock levels. It is not fragmented; rather, it serves as the umbrella for the related activities of receiving, monitoring, and replenishing. There are no other HLGs for the Warehouse Staff actor that would make this redundant. The bottom-up reconstruction is semantically identical. The granularity is appropriate for a stakeholder outcome.

low_level_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain several unsupported capabilities that go beyond the explicit documentation. Specifically, 'RecordIncomingShipmentDetails' (llg_001) and 'ScanReceivedItemBarcode' (llg_002) introduce specific data fields and hardware interactions (barcodes, manifests) not mentioned in the description, which only states that 'Goods are verified'. 'MarkPurchaseOrderAsReceived' (llg_004) implies a specific status transition for purchase orders that is not documented. 'InitiateInventoryCycleCount' (llg_007) and 'RecordInventoryCountDiscrepancy' (llg_008) introduce cycle counting and discrepancy resolution workflows that are not entailed by 'monitors inventory'. 'GenerateReplenishmentOrderProposal' (llg_010) and 'SubmitApprovedReplenishmentOrder' (llg_011) imply a complex approval and proposal workflow for replenishment that is not supported; the description only states that 'automatic replenishment can be configured'. 'TrackReplenishmentOrderStatus' (llg_012) is also unsupported as tracking is explicitly assigned to customers for deliveries, not warehouse staff for replenishment orders. These LLGs should be removed or regenerated to strictly align with the documented capabilities of verifying goods, monitoring inventory levels, and configuring/managing automatic replenishment.

branch_007.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently manage complete in-store sales transactions' accurately captures the Store Clerk's primary responsibility as defined in the actor description ('Assists customers with in-store purchases, processes payments, and handles immediate sales'). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Process Customer Purchases' is less precise as it does not explicitly distinguish in-store from online contexts or emphasize the transactional management aspect. The original goal is appropriately scoped as an end-to-end workflow for the Store Clerk, covering assistance, payment, and completion. branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Conveniently purchase products online' is supported by the project description, which states that customers can purchase products online. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Customers to Shop for Products Online' captures the same stakeholder intention. The goal is distinct from the sibling goal 'Accurately track order deliveries', as purchasing (browsing, selecting, buying, paying) is a separate functional outcome from tracking (monitoring status after purchase). There is no broader sibling goal that encompasses the entire online shopping lifecycle (from browsing to payment) for the Customer actor. Therefore, the goal is independently scoped and should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs cover browsing, viewing details, cart management (add, update, remove), initiating checkout, and selecting shipping address. However, the project description explicitly states that customers 'pay through multiple methods'. The current LLGs stop at 'Proceed to checkout' and 'Select shipping address', omitting the essential capability of actually selecting a payment method and completing the payment transaction. Without a goal for payment selection/processing, the 'purchase' is not complete. This is a material omission of an explicitly documented capability.

branch_002.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Accurately track order deliveries' is supported by the project description, which states that customers can 'track deliveries'. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Customers to Monitor Their Order Status and Delivery' captures the same stakeholder intention. This goal is distinct from the sibling goal 'Conveniently purchase products online', as tracking delivery is a post-purchase activity separate from the browsing and purchasing process. There is no broader sibling goal for the Customer actor that encompasses the entire post-purchase lifecycle (tracking) as a single umbrella; rather, 'Conveniently purchase products online' covers the pre-purchase and purchase phases, while 'Accurately track order deliveries' covers the post-purchase phase. These are independently satisfiable stakeholder outcomes (buying vs. tracking). Therefore, the goal is appropriately scoped and should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs include 'Receive delivery notifications' (llg_004), which is not explicitly supported by the project description. The description states that customers can 'track deliveries' but does not mention automatic alerts, notifications, or push messages for status changes. While notifications are a common feature in e-commerce, the instructions strictly prohibit inferring notifications unless explicitly entailed by the documentation. Therefore, llg_004 is an unsupported addition. The other LLGs (viewing history, tracking status, viewing details) are supported by the goal to 'track deliveries' and 'monitor real-time status'.

branch_003.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently manage customer support requests' is fully supported by the project description, which states that 'Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms.' The actor 'Customer Support Agent' is explicitly described as managing these requests. The goal captures the end-to-end functional outcome for this actor (receiving, categorizing, processing, and resolving tickets). There are no sibling goals for the Customer Support Agent that would make this goal redundant or fragmented. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Process Customer Support Tickets' is semantically equivalent but slightly less comprehensive than the original, which includes 'efficiently manage' and 'requests' (broader than just tickets, though tickets are the mechanism). The original goal is well-scoped, supported, and represents a distinct stakeholder intention. Therefore, it should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain several capabilities that are not explicitly supported by the project description. Specifically, 'Assign ticket to self' (llg_002) is unsupported because the description states tickets have 'automatic assignment', implying the system handles assignment, not the agent manually taking ownership. 'Add note to ticket' (llg_004) is unsupported as the description does not mention internal notes, comments, or documentation features. 'Categorize support ticket' (llg_005) is unsupported because while the HLG description mentions 'categorize', the project description only lists 'automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms' as the specific ticketing features, and 'categorize' is not explicitly entailed by the system's documented capabilities for the agent (unlike assignment or reassignment). 'Update ticket status' (llg_003) is borderline but 'response deadlines' implies status tracking, so it is likely supported. 'View new support tickets' (llg_001) is supported by the need to manage requests. Due to the unsupported nature of llg_002, llg_004, and llg_005, regeneration is required to align strictly with the documented 'automatic assignment', 'response deadlines', and 'reassignment mechanisms'.

branch_004.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Gain comprehensive business insights' is fully supported by the project description, which states that 'Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.' The actor description also explicitly aligns with this. The goal represents a distinct, end-to-end stakeholder outcome (business intelligence/analysis) that is separate from the operational goals of other actors (like managing inventory or support tickets). It is not a fragment of another goal but a complete intention for the Manager role. The reconstruction 'Enable Business Performance Monitoring and Analysis' is semantically equivalent and also supported, but the original is precise and well-scoped. No other HLG for the Manager exists to make this redundant or fragmented. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain two unsupported capabilities. 'Export business data to CSV' (llg_004) is not mentioned in the project description, which only states that management can 'analyze data'. Exporting to a specific format like CSV is an implementation detail or optional feature not entailed by the documentation. 'View dashboard summary' (llg_005) is also not explicitly supported; while 'analyze data' implies viewing information, a specific 'dashboard' with 'key business metrics and performance indicators' is a specific UI/feature construct not documented. The description mentions analyzing data concerning orders, sales, inventory, and customer support. The existing LLGs cover sales (llg_001), inventory (llg_002), and customer support (llg_003). However, the parent goal explicitly includes 'orders' as a domain for analysis. There is no LLG specifically for analyzing or viewing order data (distinct from sales performance, which might be aggregated revenue, whereas order data could include volume, status, etc.). While 'sales report' might cover some order aspects, the explicit mention of 'orders' in the description ('analyze data concerning orders, sales...') suggests a distinct capability or at least a gap if 'sales' is interpreted strictly as revenue. More critically, the unsupported LLGs (export and dashboard) violate the constraint against inferring undocumented features. Therefore, regeneration is required to remove unsupported LLGs and ensure order analysis is explicitly covered if not subsumed by sales.

branch_006.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Warehouse Inventory' accurately captures the end-to-end functional outcome for the Warehouse Staff actor. The project description explicitly states that 'Goods are verified when they arrive at stores' and 'Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured.' The actor description confirms these three core responsibilities: verifying incoming goods, monitoring inventory, and managing replenishment. The bottom-up reconstruction matches the original goal, indicating that the decomposition correctly supports this umbrella intention. There are no other HLGs for the Warehouse Staff actor that would make this goal redundant or fragmented. The goal is supported, appropriately scoped, and aligns with the stakeholder's primary objective. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) contain several capabilities that are not explicitly supported by the project description or the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) description. Specifically: 1) 'RecordIncomingShipmentDetails' (llg_001) and 'MarkPurchaseOrderAsReceived' (llg_004) imply detailed procurement workflow management (manifests, PO status) which is not mentioned in the text; the text only states 'Goods are verified when they arrive'. 2) 'ScanReceivedItemBarcode' (llg_002) assumes a specific technology (barcodes) not mentioned in the documentation. 3) 'InitiateInventoryCycleCount' (llg_007) and 'RecordInventoryCountDiscrepancy' (llg_008) introduce specific inventory audit processes (cycle counts, discrepancy logging) that are not entailed by 'monitors inventory'. 4) 'GenerateInventoryStatusReport' (llg_006) is a reporting function that overlaps with the Manager's HLG 'Gain comprehensive business insights' (which explicitly includes analyzing inventory data), and is not explicitly assigned to Warehouse Staff in the description. 5) 'GenerateReplenishmentOrderProposal' (llg_010) and 'SubmitApprovedReplenishmentOrder' (llg_011) imply a complex approval and proposal workflow for replenishment that is not described; the text only says 'automatic replenishment can be configured'. The essential capabilities explicitly supported are verifying incoming goods (updating stock), monitoring inventory (retrieving levels, identifying low stock), and managing replenishment (configuring/triggering it). The current LLGs over-specify the workflow and include unsupported audit/reporting features.

low_level_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) contain several capabilities that are not explicitly supported by the project description or the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) description. Specifically: 1) 'RecordIncomingShipmentDetails' (llg_001) and 'MarkPurchaseOrderAsReceived' (llg_004) imply detailed procurement workflow management (manifests, PO status) which is not mentioned in the text; the text only states 'Goods are verified when they arrive'. 2) 'ScanReceivedItemBarcode' (llg_002) assumes a specific technology (barcodes) not mentioned in the documentation. 3) 'InitiateInventoryCycleCount' (llg_007) and 'RecordInventoryCountDiscrepancy' (llg_008) introduce specific inventory audit processes (cycle counts, discrepancy logging) that are not entailed by 'monitors inventory'. 4) 'GenerateInventoryStatusReport' (llg_006) is a reporting function that overlaps with the Manager's HLG 'Gain comprehensive business insights' (which explicitly includes analyzing inventory data), and is not explicitly assigned to Warehouse Staff in the description. 5) 'GenerateReplenishmentOrderProposal' (llg_010) and 'SubmitApprovedReplenishmentOrder' (llg_011) imply a complex approval and proposal workflow for replenishment that is not described; the text only says 'automatic replenishment can be configured'. The essential capabilities explicitly supported are verifying incoming goods (updating stock), monitoring inventory (retrieving levels, identifying low stock), and managing replenishment (configuring/triggering it). The current LLGs over-specify the workflow and include unsupported audit/reporting features.
low_level_evaluation.regeneration_feedback: Remove unsupported specific workflow steps (barcodes, cycle counts, discrepancy logs, PO status updates, replenishment proposals/approvals) and reporting features that belong to the Manager. Focus on the explicitly stated capabilities: verifying incoming goods (updating stock levels upon receipt), monitoring inventory (retrieving current stock, identifying items below reorder points), and managing replenishment (configuring automatic replenishment rules or triggering replenishment based on stock levels).

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Conveniently purchase products online' accurately captures the Customer's intention to browse, select, and buy products. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Customers to Shop for Products Online' is semantically equivalent. The goal is distinct from the sibling goal 'Accurately track order deliveries', as purchasing (transactional) and tracking (post-transactional) represent independent stakeholder outcomes. The description supports this goal, and the granularity is appropriate for a High-Level Goal. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs cover browsing, viewing details, cart management (add, update, remove), initiating checkout, and selecting a shipping address. However, the project description explicitly states that customers 'pay through multiple methods'. The current LLGs stop at 'Proceed to checkout' and 'Select shipping address', omitting the essential capability of actually processing or selecting a payment method to finalize the purchase. Without a goal related to payment, the 'purchase' aspect of the HLG is incomplete. Therefore, a material omission exists.

branch_005.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Product Proposals' is well-supported by the project description, which states that 'Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department.' The goal correctly captures the end-to-end lifecycle for the Supplier actor: creating, submitting, and monitoring the status of proposals. It is not fragmented, as it encompasses the entire workflow for this specific artifact (product proposals) from the supplier's perspective. There are no other HLGs for the Supplier actor that would make this redundant. The reconstruction 'Manage Supplier Product Proposals' is semantically equivalent but slightly less descriptive of the intent than the original. The original goal is precise, supported, and appropriately scoped. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain several capabilities that are not explicitly supported by the project description. Specifically, 'Create a new product proposal draft' (llg_001) and 'Add product details to a proposal draft' (llg_002) imply a multi-step draft creation process with specific fields, whereas the description only states that 'Suppliers submit proposals'. While creating a proposal is entailed, the specific 'draft' state and granular 'add details' step are not documented. More critically, 'Attach supporting documents to a proposal draft' (llg_003) is entirely unsupported; the description makes no mention of file uploads, images, or certifications. Additionally, 'View evaluation feedback for a rejected proposal' (llg_007) is redundant with 'Retrieve the detailed status of a specific product proposal' (llg_006) which already includes feedback, and the specific focus on 'rejected' proposals is not explicitly distinguished in the documentation from general status monitoring. The core supported capabilities are submitting proposals and monitoring their status/feedback. The unsupported draft management and document attachment features constitute material defects.

branch_008.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. It is distinct from the sibling goal 'Manage System Configurations' and does not overlap with other actors' goals. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Administer Supplier Proposal Selection' is semantically equivalent but slightly less descriptive of the strategic outcome ('optimal selection') than the original. The current LLGs cover the core workflow of retrieving proposals (llg_001, llg_002), evaluating them (llg_003), and making a selection decision (llg_004, llg_005). The description states that 'Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department' and that 'Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.' missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale:
Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The current High-Level Goals comprehensively cover all explicit functional requirements and actor responsibilities defined in the project description. 

1. **Supplier**: 'Manage Product Proposals' covers the submission and monitoring of proposals.
2. **Administrator**: 'Ensure optimal supplier selection' covers the evaluation of proposals. 'Manage System Configurations' covers the explicit requirement to manage system configurations.
3. **Warehouse Staff**: 'Manage Warehouse Inventory' covers verifying incoming goods, monitoring inventory, and managing replenishment.
4. **Customer**: 'Conveniently purchase products online' covers browsing and buying. 'Accurately track order deliveries' covers delivery tracking. Payment processing is an integral part of the purchase transaction covered by the purchase HLG.
5. **Customer Support Agent**: 'Efficiently manage customer support requests' covers the ticketing system, assignment, and resolution mechanisms.
6. **Manager**: 'Gain comprehensive business insights' covers the analysis of orders, sales, inventory, and support data.
7. **Store Clerk**: 'Efficiently manage complete in-store sales transactions' covers in-store assistance, sales, and payments.

All retired goals were either redundant, overly granular (LLG-level), or subsumed by the broader, more accurate current HLGs. No documented actor-level outcome is left uncovered.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Accurately track order deliveries' is fully supported by the project description, which explicitly states that customers can 'track deliveries'. It represents a distinct, independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome separate from the act of purchasing (covered by 'Conveniently purchase products online'). While the bottom-up reconstruction suggests a broader 'Track and Monitor Orders', the original goal is precise, correctly scoped to the delivery phase, and does not overlap with the purchase HLG in a way that makes it redundant. It is a valid, atomic HLG for the Customer actor. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs include 'Receive delivery notifications' (llg_004), which is not supported by the project description. The documentation states that customers can 'track deliveries' but does not mention automatic notifications, alerts, or push messages for status changes. According to the evaluation guidelines, conventional but undocumented additions like notifications must be removed. The other LLGs (viewing history, tracking status, viewing details) are supported by the ability to 'track deliveries' and 'purchase products online' (which implies having an order history to track). Therefore, the decomposition requires regeneration to remove the unsupported notification capability.
